title: 六级：地名翻译与人物声音
instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question. 每篇五题，每题只选一项；全部材料与问题均需作答。
source_notice: 参照已核考试院2016大纲及完整样题：每篇五题、每题四候选，四级每篇300—350词、六级400—450词；单篇完整练习与整节两篇十题分列，不把单篇冒充整节。本文城镇、机构、人物、事件与研究均为原创虚构，按文意作答，不作现实事实。旧官方样题原键既有风险保留，不当独立gold；本稿逐项依据与干扰反证为作者自审，独立教研、学生、商用及生产未验证，不证明产品档位人群等值。

passages.text:
The translator of a fictional novel set in the invented region of Selna encounters a difficulty before completing the opening chapter. A hill outside the main town has a name that can mean either “shelter” or “concealment”, depending on who uses it. The town’s inhabitants disagree about an event associated with that hill. Choosing a single English equivalent would therefore appear to settle a disagreement that the novel itself deliberately sustains.

An editor initially recommends “Shelter Hill”. It is easy to pronounce, looks convincing on the map printed inside the book, and gives readers a phrase they can remember. The translator objects that this fluency comes at a cost. A character who describes the hill as a place where evidence was hidden would seem to be arguing against a reassuring official name. In the original, the character is also making use of a second meaning already present in the same word. Translation would change the resources available to that voice.

Retaining the Selna name offers another possibility, but not a perfect escape from interpretation. English readers would no longer hear either everyday meaning immediately. A glossary could explain both, yet consulting it would interrupt scenes in which the name occurs casually. Printing the name in italics might draw attention to its unfamiliarity even when, for the characters, it is an entirely ordinary part of the landscape. Each solution directs attention somewhere and away from something else.

The translator eventually keeps the original name, explains the two meanings in a brief introductory note, and lets later dialogue bring out their different associations. The editor accepts this arrangement after seeing a revised chapter. They do not add an explanation every time the hill appears. The aim is to give readers enough orientation to follow the disagreement without converting each mention into a lesson about language.

This decision does not establish a rule that place names should always remain unchanged. A name serving only to locate a journey might present a different problem. Here, the important task is to preserve the possibility of competing interpretations, rather than to preserve every visible feature of the original word. The translator describes her work as arranging a relationship among name, narrative and reader. An apparently convenient equivalent can alter that relationship; an unfamiliar expression can also distort it if its unfamiliarity is made more prominent than the story requires. Fidelity, in this case, involves deciding which difference the translation must allow readers to notice.

questions.stem: Why is the hill’s name difficult to translate?
options: A
Its competing meanings participate in a disagreement within the novel.
B
The author has supplied several inconsistent maps of the region.
C
No character in the novel can pronounce the name correctly.
D
English readers already associate it with a real historical event.
questions.evidence: a disagreement that the novel itself deliberately sustains

candidate_reasons.A: 双义与人物争论共同构成难题，A准确
candidate_reasons.B: 一张书内地图，未说多张矛盾
candidate_reasons.C: 发音便利是英语编辑考虑，不是人物发不出
candidate_reasons.D: 地域情节虚构，未假设现实历史联想

questions.stem: What is the translator’s objection to “Shelter Hill”?
options: A
It would prevent a map from being included in the book.
B
It would make every character use an unfamiliar foreign expression.
C
It could change how a character’s challenge is understood.
D
It would require the original author to remove the hill from the plot.
questions.evidence: Translation would change the resources available to that voice

candidate_reasons.B: Shelter Hill是流畅英语，非外语化
candidate_reasons.C: 由词内双义变成反驳温暖官方名，改变人物挑战，C正确

questions.stem: What is the purpose of discussing italics?
options: A
To show that readers prefer typographical explanations to glossaries.
B
To illustrate how retaining a word may still alter its narrative effect.
C
To prove that the original name has only one ordinary meaning.
D
To establish that editors should control all translation decisions.

candidate_reasons.B: 原词对人物日常却对英语读者突出陌生，保留形式也改变效果
candidate_reasons.D: 讨论选择效果，非编辑独占决策

questions.stem: How does the adopted solution manage explanation?
options: A
It places a full definition beside every later occurrence of the name.
B
It removes dialogue that draws attention to conflicting memories.
C
It leaves readers without any account of the name’s meanings.
D
It supplies initial orientation and allows the dialogue to develop the contrast.
questions.evidence: lets later dialogue bring out their different associations

candidate_reasons.B: 保留人物对话承载不同联想
candidate_reasons.D: 简短前言引导，后续对话展开，D准确

questions.stem: What does the final paragraph suggest about fidelity in translation?
options: A
It requires identical visible forms regardless of a word’s role.
B
It may depend on preserving the interpretive work a feature performs.
C
It can be achieved by always choosing the most fluent equivalent.
D
It requires making every foreign expression conspicuously unfamiliar.
questions.evidence: which difference the translation must allow readers to notice

candidate_reasons.A: 明确不是保留每个可见形式
candidate_reasons.B: 保留名字使竞争解释可能的作用，B概括
candidate_reasons.C: 方便流畅可能改变关系，非总选
candidate_reasons.D: 陌生感过分突出也扭曲叙事
